slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that make your mind
frighteningly sharp

arguing the other side

once a week, write the strongest version of an opinion you disagree with. understanding the other side properly makes your own arguments far harder to beat.

one idea a day

i used to read only headlines and pretend i understood. learning one real idea a day, a theory or an experiment, changed how i think more than any book ever did.
slides.texte_sophia:
one idea a day

i used to read only headlines. now i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app: a theory, an experiment, a turning point. my thinking has never been sharper.

slides.texte_overlay:
reading the original

read the actual speech, letter or study instead of an article about it. going straight to the source is slower, but you'll notice what everyone else missed.

chess puzzles

solve one chess puzzle a day with your morning coffee. thinking a few moves ahead trains the same calm and careful logic you'll use in every big decision.

teaching a child

explain one hard idea a week as if to a ten year old. if you can't make it simple, you've found exactly the part you don't really understand properly yet.
